findings.title: New storage canary requires an unrequested same-origin API URL
findings.quote: capture the current revision plus that successful update's actual absolute same-origin URL, method, relevant headers and body
findings.counterexample: A conforming UI at http://localhost:3000 can send its library requests to http://127.0.0.1:3000 on the same required Express process and SQLite database, with working CORS. It implements text-only storage and all Save semantics, but its actual observed update URL is not same-origin with the UI. S21 cannot obtain the requested setup URL without inventing a route/origin, and the new canary can lose credit for architecture that the public brief permits.
findings.impact: Bounded false-fail risk for cw_save_load_execution_canary (weight 0.20 of 32.70). Above the floor its maximum shaped reward mass is 0.0036697248; this is arithmetic, not a measured app score.
findings.fix: Use the actual absolute observed URL served by the permitted local app, preserving its method, headers, body and origin/CORS behavior; do not require the API URL to share the UI origin.
findings.evidence_status: The prompt restriction and absent public requirement are directly source-confirmed; the conforming loopback-alias app is a reasoned alternative, not an executed fixture.

repair_assessments.topic: S24 invalid NEW creation versus update validation
repair_assessments.reason: S24 now exercises exact/padded collisions and empty/whitespace titles on both NEW and current-revision update formats. It explicitly captures the successful creation format, forbids adding a stale revision to creation, uses otherwise-valid fields, requires fresh unchanged complete records/revisions and no new identity, and retains valid creation/update/recovery controls. An app validating only PUT while accepting invalid POST titles is distinguished. The golden POST and PUT both call fields() and uniqueTitle() before mutation. These source observations do not replace browser execution.

repair_assessments.reason: Both successive trials remain in S23 with editor roles reversed, exact dirty title/filename/source retention, actual UI conflict/prevention, server replay only when UI prevention suppresses a request, latest-revision reload, deliberate reapplication and fresh exact readback under the same identity. repair_assessments.topic: New error-family, loop and duration coverage
repair_assessments.verdict: Pass within inspected source scope, runtime not exercised
repair_assessments.reason: Finite braced/unbraced/Promise loop controls distinguish an instrumenter that aborts every loop. Complete-HTML timer and primitive Promise fixtures require document line 6; JS primitive rejection requires line 2. Successful quick/delayed duration comparison defeats a constant duration label, and terminal-duration credit reuses failed/stopped/timed-out observations. These demands follow supported source execution, authored source lines and each-run duration in the public notes; no exact API route, label, package, clock unit or unsupported execution family is added. Current runtime source adds primitive rejection origin tracking, but its browser correctness and full input space remain unmeasured in this review.

two_way_coverage.reverse_grounding: Creation and update are both saved snippet operations. Exact/padded duplicate, empty/space, trimmed success and case-distinct success follow the public title rule. No new title length rule is graded.

Exact line fixtures operationalize one-based user-source and complete-document line numbers. Primitive reasons are valid source, not an additional unsupported execution family. Separate recovery follows the usable playground and fresh Run promises.
Each run includes success, failure, Stop and timeout. Coarse units/rounding/overhead are allowed, and the delayed positive fixture supplies a distinguishing measurement.
Finite literal loops are necessary success controls for the promised source-written loop support. Existing negative fixtures still measure time-limit enforcement.

The monitor/carrier side-effect probe addresses a bounded observable consequence of server evaluation. It cannot establish the universal server non-evaluation claim; the same-origin setup restriction is ungrounded (RC-01).

coverage_limitations.topic: Storage canary is bounded evidence only
coverage_limitations.detail: A server that evaluates snippets in a restricted realm without fetch, catches execution errors, or evaluates only unprobed source can leave this monitor unchanged. A browser matching-write control proves request validity in the browser, not that every possible server evaluation environment could issue it. The prompt accurately discloses the limit, so do not relabel the historical absolute non-evaluation assurance as fully verified. No private-source grading should be added.

coverage_limitations.topic: S09 last-good refresh must be interpreted after the new controls
coverage_limitations.detail: The three successful JS controls can replace lastGood with a blank fresh document. Line 244 requires establishing a completed DOM/log render afterward. The older next-step wording about reusing S08 must mean rerunning that source or otherwise establishing a currently completed render, not comparing rollback to a historical render displaced by the finite controls. Make this explicit if revising again; record the actual current render. The explicit after-controls instruction prevents treating this as a confirmed false-fail by itself.

workload.interpretation: 58 to 64 adds four recovery result rows without repeating their scenarios, one terminal-duration row reusing existing terminal observations, and one new storage-canary flow. Independent of row count, S09 adds three finite Runs, S12 adds an HTML timer error, S13 adds two rejection Runs, and S24 adds four invalid NEW submissions/readbacks. Duration collection adds timed readbacks and only a conditional extra delayed Run. The stored prompt grows by 5504 UTF-8 bytes and judge TOML by 2813 bytes; these are source sizes, not resolved CLI argument size or latency. Printed action estimates rise from 396 to 436, including S01 +12 with unchanged S01 procedure. S21 still prints 18 despite added monitor/carrier creation, updates, load/readbacks and request capture; therefore the summed estimates are not a measured or complete action count. Full workload fit cannot be inferred from count64 or 9000 seconds.
